- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤-0.5) within 3–5 days, model often fails to correct downward; apply downward bias of 2–5% to forecast.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, consider mean reversion; reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals (e.g., +1, -1, +1), model often misreads trend; align forecast with sentiment direction, not absolute magnitude.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility; use 14-day moving average as baseline for smoothing.
